findings.new_evidence: Round 2 push-back rationale: 'Without the requirement, a reviewer reading the PRD has no record that the fallback's surface is widening from 4 to 8 kinds.' But the revised R10 (line 90) reads: 'Unsupported block kinds (anything outside the eight listed) continue to render as <pre> with the existing "Unsupported visual block" warning, never silently dropped. The new blocks expand the supported list; the unknown-block fallback's surface widens to eight but its behaviour is unchanged.' The 'surface widens to eight' commitment is fully captured by R12/AC-16 (line 98 onwards: 'Update all hardcoded references to the four-kind supported list … all four call-sites must update to the eight-kind list in lockstep; the post-change file has zero references to the four-kind-only set'). R12 is the substantive widening commitment; R10 is its conditional-mirror restating that the fallback behaviour didn't change. Additionally, AC-8 (line 161-163) tests for a `:::xyzzy` fallback — but the test is identical regardless of whether the supported list has 4 or 8 kinds; nothing about AC-8 verifies the widening, only the unchanged fallback. The push-back's claim ('the requirement-level commitment to the widened surface') is actually carried by R12, not R10.
findings.claim: R10 + AC-8 are still defensive restatement once R12/AC-16 entered the PRD. The widening commitment lives in R12 ('all four call-sites must update to the eight-kind list … the post-change file has zero references to the four-kind-only set') and AC-16 (line 225-229: '! grep -nE … the four-kind-only set'). R10 + AC-8 verify that the unchanged unknown-block fallback still works for non-supported kinds — pure regression coverage of an existing rule. Two requirements/ACs covering the same widening scope is a redundancy the surgical-changes lens flags. Severity is now 'note' (not 'block' or 'concern'): the harm is small (a defensive but harmless requirement) and the push-back has rhetorical merit, but the redundancy with R12/AC-16 makes R10 demote-able rather than indispensable.
findings.proposed_change: Either: (a) demote R10 to a single sentence inside R12 ('R12 also implicitly preserves the unknown-block fallback at brief/SKILL.md:214 for kinds outside the eight'), and fold AC-8's grep into AC-16 (negative assertion: 'a `:::xyzzy` fixture compiles to a <pre> carrying "Unsupported visual block"'); or (b) keep R10/AC-8 but add an explicit cross-reference at the top of R10 noting that the widening commitment is R12's job and R10 is the regression-coverage clause. Pick (a) for surgical economy, (b) for explicit traceability. Either way, eliminate the redundancy in the surface that two requirements both claim authorship of.
